items.title: Albanese will today try to defend his prime-time message
items.description: With no realistic end in sight and a whole lot of economic pain still to come, the PM's decision to make a direct plea to the nation was not one taken lightly.

items.title: Trump says he's considering pulling US out of 'paper tiger' NATO
items.description: Donald Trump says he is strongly considering pulling the United States out of NATO after allies failed to back US military action against Iran, in an interview with the UK's Daily Telegraph.

items.title: Iran war may depend on who runs out of missiles and interceptors first
items.description: Analysts estimate the US is burning through high-end weapons in Iran at a rate that could take years to replenish, risking the West's military readiness for other potential conflicts.

items.title: Australia wasting talent of migrants on an 'industrial scale', experts say
items.description: Australia is failing to recognise the qualifications of highly trained permanent migrants, former Treasury secretary Martin Parkinson says.

items.title: One Nation picked candidates accused of domestic abuse, antisemitism
items.description: A One Nation candidate in the South Australian election was accused of domestic abuse, bullying and harassment, while another made racist, antisemitic and homophobic social media posts, raising fresh questions about the party's vetting processes as it surges in popularity.

items.title: Next generation heads for the Moon
items.description: If all goes well for NASA's Artemis II mission, the astronauts aboard could fly the furthest that humans have ever gone. What should we be looking out for?

items.title: Almost 50 French cities have free public transport. What can Australia learn?
items.description: There are growing calls in Australia for free public transport amid the Iran war with two states putting in place free services on a temporary basis. But in France, almost 50 cities have free public transport.

items.title: Singapore's biggest oil source is blocked and experts warn Australians will pay
items.description: Singapore is exposed to the oil shock from Iran’s effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and its response will shape the fuel crisis in Australia.

items.title: 'Dance for me': Australian Harrods survivor tells of Mohamed Al Fayed abuse
items.description: Jessica tried to keep her distance from Harrods billionaire owner Mohamed Al Fayed, who was known to abuse his female staff, until he spotted her going down an escalator.

items.title: Labor calls for investigation into Hellyer mine allegations
items.description: Labor has called on the Tasmanian government to investigate allegations a metals mine, when under a previous ownership, was being used by organised crime affiliates to launder money.

items.title: Keep track of today's sharp drop in petrol prices around the country
items.description: The federal government's cut to fuel excise has almost immediately flowed through to petrol prices at the pump, according to ABC tracking of fuel price data nationwide.

items.title: 'Lack of transparency endemic' in university sector, union warns
items.description: Victorian universities are abusing Freedom Of Information laws, according to one union, as transparency concerns grow. The claim follows a Four Corners investigation that revealed universities spent $1.8 billion on consultants in one year.

items.title: Weather to deliver Easter treat, but another cyclone looms next week
items.description: Australia has just been soaked by its third wettest February-March on record, but for most of the country, skies have cleared up just in time for Easter.

items.title: The big gamble Andy Griffiths took to become a world-famous kids' author
items.description: Andy Griffiths has written 43 books, is the Children's Laureate, and is about to turn his Treehouse series into an ABC TV show. So what inspires the former punk and teacher to keep creating quirky tales for kids?

items.title: Museum fans: Test yourself with our curious collection of trivia
items.description: Australia’s museums hold a treasure trove of odd facts, native animals and even burlesque history. So how much do you know about the things hidden in our nation’s vaults?

items.title: Study shows gen Z craves in-person connection more than other generations
items.description: Gen Z is embracing retro technology like iPods, vinyl and Polaroid cameras and craves in-person connection more than any other generation, according to a Live Nation study.

items.title: Parents demand action after concrete fell into Melbourne classroom
items.description: Collingwood College is sending students to another campus for science classes after concrete fell from its water-damaged roof and forced the closure of an entire floor of its main building.

items.title: Despite rising fuel costs, the Sydney Royal Easter Show must go on
items.description: The country has come to the city for the Royal Easter Show and despite the cost of the trip blowing out amid high fuel prices, the exhibitors say they would not miss it.

items.title: Unions push for Queensland to raise working age for children
items.description: The state government is conducting a sunset review of the child employment regulations that stipulate the rules for kids who work in Queensland.

items.title: Staff accused of stealing $1m from Village Roadshow
items.description: Village Roadshow allege more than $1 million in inappropriate payments had already been identified "with the total amount likely to increase as the investigation continues".

items.title: Former Sydney University lecturer seen in Iran video about Hormuz Strait
items.description: An Australian academic has appeared in an Iranian propaganda video supporting a toll system imposed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on foreign merchant shipping.

items.title: Robotaxi malfunction in China causes traffic chaos as cars stall
items.description: Videos on social media showed cars stopped in the middle of multi-lane roads with their hazard lights on obstructing traffic.

items.title: Sixers force NBL title decider after beating Kings in cliffhanger
items.description: Torrey Craig's missed free throw for the Sydney Kings in the dying seconds allows the Adelaide 36ers to level the NBL championship series at 2-2 with a gripping 92-91 win.

items.title: Arnold carried in jubilant scenes after Iraq qualifies for World Cup
items.description: Former Socceroos coach Graham Arnold has guided Iraq to their first FIFA World Cup appearance in 40 years with a playoff win over Bolivia.

items.title: At least four killed in daytime Russian drone strikes across Ukraine
items.description: Both sides are launching drone attacks as the war between Russia and Ukraine drags into its fifth year.
